title: Released Windows updater locks its own console launcher
signatures: failed to remove file[^\r\n]*Scripts[/\\]hermes\.exe[^\r\n]*Access is denied\. \(os error 5\)
Git update failed[^\r\n]*'pip', 'install', '-e', '\.'[^\r\n]*returned non-zero exit status 2
explanation: The March/April Windows updater is already running from hermes.exe when uv tries to replace it. Windows refuses the locked launcher. The update target cannot change that loaded code; re-running the installer is a separate recovery route.

title: Script installs offer a manual update instead of an app hand-off
errors: ^E2E ASSERTION FAILED: app driven via captured hermes desktop spec; update completed$
^E2E ASSERTION FAILED: GUI driver clicked Update now and the app quit for hand-off$
signatures: \[updates\] no staged updater; surfacing manual `hermes update` for CLI install at
explanation: A Windows script install leaves no staged updater, so the app's Update button explicitly returns manual: hermes update without starting a hand-off and never writes the result file the driver polls for. Confirmed in the released code for v2026.7.1 and again for v2026.8.3 (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts returns { ok: true, manual: true } on the no-staged-updater branch). Desktop-installer installs have a staged-updater path and are not covered by this exception.

title: Released Windows updater cannot replace a native extension it has already imported
signatures: failed to remove file[^\r\n]*cryptography[/\\]hazmat[/\\]bindings[/\\]_rust\.pyd[^\r\n]*Access is denied\. \(os error 5\)
explanation: The August updater runs in a Python process that has already imported cryptography, so cryptography/hazmat/bindings/_rust.pyd is mapped into the running interpreter. The update target raises the cryptography floor to 50.x, so uv must replace that exact .pyd and Windows refuses. The loaded extension module belongs to the starting release's process; no change in the update target can unload it. Re-running the installer is a separate tested recovery route. This is the loaded-module analogue of windows-launcher-self-lock and does not cover an access-denied error on any other file. The CLI updater is the same released code whichever way the install was produced, so all three install methods are covered here -- unlike the app-button exception, where a desktop-installer install really does take a different (staged-updater) path.
